title: Love people
hook: asked about humaneness, Confucius said: love people (Analects 12.22)
carry: he didn't ask about the horses

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was upekkha, an even heart that loves without clinging. Your line was even-hearted. Today the path moves east, to Chinese voices on love.

What does it mean to be humane? A student named Fan Chi put that question to his teacher. Not a question about the stars, or the gods, or how to get ahead: just the meaning of one word. The teacher was Confucius, and his answer, in plain English, comes to two words. The conversation is in the Analects, a book of his sayings that tradition says his followers gathered.

The word is ren. It's been translated as benevolence, humaneness, goodness, perfect virtue. In James Legge's old translation, Fan Chi asked about benevolence, and "The Master said, 'It is to love all men.'" Love people. Not an idea of people: people themselves, starting with the ones in front of you. In the same passage, Fan Chi also asks about knowledge, and the answer matches: know people. The Analects keeps one small scene that shows ren better than a definition. The stables burned while Confucius was away at court. When he came home, he asked whether anyone had been hurt. The text adds that he didn't ask about the horses. For Confucius, love grows outward through real relationships: parents, siblings, friends, neighbors, rulers and the ruled. Another saying in the Analects describes the humane person as one who, wanting to stand firm, helps others stand firm too. Love here isn't mainly a feeling. It's a way of treating people, practiced in a household, then a street, then a whole society: ordinary conduct, done humanely, again and again.
screen: `REN: HUMANENESS.` · `IT IS TO LOVE ALL MEN.` · `HE DIDN'T ASK ABOUT THE HORSES.` · `REN STARTS CLOSE.` · then, large: `LOVE PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: Think back over the last day for one moment when someone was treated as a means to an end, by you or toward you, a cashier, a coworker, someone on the phone, and just see it, without judging. Then choose one person you'll meet and one small way to treat them humanely, their name, a real question, your full patience, and hold that intention for the rest of the sit.
Ren. Humaneness in the Analects, which Confucius explained to Fan Chi in plain words: love people. Today's word.
Your line: he didn't ask about the horses. His question was about people. Day eight hundred fifty.

howItsDone: In Confucian tradition, ren (humaneness) is practiced through everyday relationships: honoring family, keeping faith with friends, and treating others with care.
